chunks: Ali ibn Abdullah al-Varraq - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdil Salam ibn Salih al-Harawi
He said: By God! Ar-Ridha’ (peace be upon him) did not accept this affair willingly. He was unwillingly taken to Kufa, then he was taken to Marv by way of Basra and Fars.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Ridha (the title of Imam Ali ibn Musa)
key_terms.الْبَصْرَةِ: Basra (a major city in southern Iraq)
key_terms.مَرْو: Marv (a city in Khurasan, present-day Turkmenistan)

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Ridha (a.s.) accept the caliphate willingly or under duress?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the political coercion exerted by the Abbasid Caliph Al-Ma'mun, who forced Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) into the role of heir apparent to legitimize his rule. The specific route of transfer—through Kufa, Basra, and Fars to Marv—underscores the strategic movement of the Imam through key Iraqi and Persian centers, emphasizing that his acceptance was a calculated political necessity rather than a voluntary endorsement of Abbasid authority.
